_comment: Reference-value ledger for confer.to (Confer Labs / Moxie Marlinspike): a private-AI assistant on a GPU confidential VM (Intel TDX preferred, SEV-SNP fallback) that runs vLLM in-enclave and provisions ephemeral, attested GCP-TDX exec-worker VMs for document tools + code execution. Each row's `signoff` is either `analyst-pair` (a human reviewer promoted it; audited_by lists them) or `agent-draft-baseline` (an agent-draft review awaiting promotion). This ledger is AGENT-DRAFT and THIN by construction: confer's inference endpoint is a Noise_XX websocket that gates the attestation handshake behind an authenticated session (no anonymous/REST attestation endpoint), so it is NOT wired into the daily probe and production manifests must be captured from a logged-in session (not yet done). Identity: the proxy image measurement carried in a Sigstore-signed manifest.json handed to the client in Noise handshake msg2. The client checks quote-RTMR == manifest.tdxMeasurements, firmware MRTD against one hardcoded value, and the manifest's KEYLESS-Sigstore signature by releases@conferlabs.iam.gserviceaccount.com -- which requires a Rekor inclusion proof to validate the short-lived Fulcio cert, so every servable image is forced into the public Rekor log (16 proxy signings as of 2026-09-02; no covert backdoor image possible). KEY WEAKNESS (Chutes class): the served MODEL and its config are on operator-attached, UNMEASURED disks (/dev/vdb weights, /dev/vdc secrets.env carrying VLLM_MODEL). Nothing extends an RTMR with them (no runtime RTMR extension in confer-image), so a matching quote attests OS + vLLM binary + proxy.jar (proxy.zip is hash-pinned via proxy-hash in the measured cmdline) -- NOT which model ran. Source-of-truth for the image = conferlabs/{confer-image,confer-proxy,confer-worker-image} (open, Nix-reproducible, tag-gated CI), but bound to the signed measurement only by a version STRING, not build provenance (cosign sign-blob, no SLSA/attest-build-provenance). Full audit: https://github.com/amiller/devproof-audits-guide/tree/main/case-studies/confer . Refresh: capture a live manifest from an authenticated session on a new imageVersion and diff RTMRs against a reproduced Nix build (verify-client/ in the case study).

audits.notes: The single firmware MRTD the browser client pins (only MRENCLAVE-style pin in the client; image RTMRs are taken from the server-sent, Confer-signed manifest, not reproduced). Two proxy-image RTMR sets are embedded in the client bundle but are NOT the enforced allowlist -- the enforced check compares quote-RTMR to the manifest: {rtmr1: 225da8c5c388cbe4f3f3b47df36b5a83e615186cd8993bac632a9704dc2974aff3518af391c9d1d481f59796483255e9, rtmr2: d4e08948700235c2fc9bce1ed5907e8bae49bdc4f3533319365d348533facb66e85472633dc3436becfb00fa09a8eb54} and {rtmr1: c5b8e201b95e3e830eee693b7401d5c214e7662bf9874e1bad1d6cf4254b5d6aefb333b368bab99770308400e3e9255b, rtmr2: f7639dc12eaf5e7ae7a0cfe9d7d6baab4342c12c9f94fbbea5f9b7b60b824b1783112a679a294b36a1e4a529c07b3ca1} (provenance-unverified).
